title: Merge sort
objective: Split the list in half, sort each half the same way, and merge two sorted lists.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): merge sort (divide and conquer)

simplifies: Each merge here makes a new list. Merge sort usually needs extra memory like this, about n items; that is its main cost compared with quick sort.

quiz.prompt: Merging [2, 7] and [3, 4] gives which list, and what is taken first?

options.explanation: Right. Compare the fronts (2 and 3), take the smaller, and repeat.
That just joins them. Merging compares the fronts each time.
The smaller front item goes first: 2 < 3.

quiz.prompt: Why is merge sort O(n log n)?

options.text: There are about log₂ n levels of halving, and merging each level takes about n steps
options.explanation: Right. log n levels × n work per level.
That would be n². Merging avoids most comparisons.

options.text: It only works on short lists
options.explanation: It works on any length; that is the point of splitting.
